blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — fondaparinux renal contraindication
stem: An adult client with a creatinine clearance of 24 mL/min has a new order for fondaparinux for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after surgery. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Administer fondaparinux as ordered because severe renal impairment does not materially alter fondaparinux clearance or increase anticoagulant exposure after prophylactic dosing.
options.B: Question the order because fondaparinux is contraindicated for VTE prophylaxis or treatment when creatinine clearance is below 30 mL/min due to reduced clearance and bleeding risk.
options.C: Request intramuscular fondaparinux instead because changing the route prevents accumulation and permits use of the same prophylactic dose in severe renal impairment.
options.D: Ask to increase the fondaparinux dose because severe renal impairment reduces anticoagulant exposure and requires additional medication to maintain thromboprophylaxis.

rationale: Current ARIXTRA prescribing information lists severe renal impairment with creatinine clearance below 30 mL/min as a contraindication for VTE prophylaxis or treatment. Fondaparinux is eliminated mainly unchanged in urine; reduced renal clearance prolongs anticoagulant exposure and increases bleeding risk. The medication is administered subcutaneously, not intramuscularly. Therefore B is correct. A and D reverse the pharmacokinetic effect of renal impairment, while C proposes an unsupported and inappropriate route change.
educational_objective: Identify severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) as a contraindication to fondaparinux for VTE prophylaxis or treatment and question the order before administration.
source_document_title: ARIXTRA (fondaparinux sodium injection) — Full Prescribing Information
source_version_date: Prescribing information revised December 2024; current DailyMed/FDA label accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: Contraindications §4: severe renal impairment, CrCl <30 mL/min. Warnings and Precautions §5.3: do not use for VTE prophylaxis or treatment when CrCl <30 mL/min; impaired renal function reduces clearance and increases bleeding risk. Clinical Pharmacology §12.4: renal impairment prolongs elimination; severe renal impairment reduces total clearance by approximately 55% versus normal renal function.
source_claim_supported: Fondaparinux is contraindicated for VTE prophylaxis or treatment when CrCl is below 30 mL/min because renal impairment reduces clearance and increases/prolongs anticoagulant exposure and bleeding risk.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: review renal laboratory data; identify contraindications and medication-related risks; administer parenteral therapies safely.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as complete renal-safety decisions of comparable length.
Preserved the exact CrCl <30 mL/min contraindication while removing the original key-length cue.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms B uniquely matches current ARIXTRA labeling. The renal threshold is directly sourced and all options are closely length-matched.
